title: Credit Market Conditions and Mental Health
eligible_reason: Two main-text tables use a binary staggered treatment with unit and region-by-year fixed effects and no controls: Table 9 (county-year CRA small-business lending, 2001-2017): reghdfe y Treat_Post, absorb(county state#year) cluster(county), where Treat_Post = Treat (county had branches of both acquirer and target in the year before a large-bank merger) x Post (after the merger), constructed following Nguyen (2019) from several mergers in different years; and Table 10 (PSID individual panel, biennial 2001-2017): reghdfe y Treat_Post [aweight=weight], absorb(individual strata state#year) cluster(county) on the low-income subsample, where strata is a gender-by-race group (time-invariant within individual, so redundant with individual FE). State-by-year FE are allowed (time-invariant characteristic x calendar time). The headline Table 2 uses the 0-4 Rice-Strahan IBBEA index (multi-valued treatment) with time-varying controls, and the Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess did_imputation in Table 3 Panel B includes time-varying state macro controls, so those are ineligible. The package ships only mock-up data.
design_notes: Main setting (Tables 2-8): NLSY79 respondents, CES-D depression score (Cal_CESTotal), state-level IBBEA deregulation index 0-4 (continuous/multi-valued) with individual controls and state macro controls, FE gender#race#year, statefip (or individual R0000100 with statefip#c.year trends), survey_month, survey_day, aweight SampleWeight, cluster statefip. Table 3 Panel B: did_imputation Cal_CESTotal R0000100 year year_ibbea_g{0,1,2,3} [aweight], controls(g_gdp_per ln_ppl census_poverty bls_r_unemp r_laborforce ln_hpi) fe(R0000100 gender#race#year survey_month survey_day) cluster(statefip): BJS imputation with binarized adoption year (first year the index reaches g) but with time-varying controls and extra survey-month/day FE (ineligible as reported; N about 6,500, 4 columns). Second setting (Tables 9-10): large regional bank mergers causing branch closures, Nguyen (2019) design; Table 9 N = 54,299 county-years, 3,208 county clusters, 900 state#year cells (approx. 50 states x 18 years, 2001-2017 per mock data); Table 10 N = 8,182 person-years, 1,883 individuals, 427 county clusters, PSID waves 2001-2017 biennial, LowIncome==1. The number of merger cohorts is not recoverable from the mock data; Nguyen (2019) uses multiple mergers across years, so at least two cohorts. Whether Treat_Post is defined from the first qualifying merger only (never switches off) must be checked with the authors; the dictionary describes a standard Treat x Post.
main_or_robustness: main (Tables 9-10 are the paper's second, merger-based identification strategy)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Merger-based Treat x Post following Nguyen (2019): several large-bank mergers in different years; exact cohort count requires the real merger list. IBBEA BJS columns use state deregulation years 1994-2005 (multiple cohorts) but are ineligible because of controls.
never_treated_note: Counties / individuals never exposed to a qualifying merger serve as controls (Treat = 0).
modern_estimators_named: borusyak_jaravel_spiess (did_imputation), Table 3 Panel B, with time-varying controls
preferred_spec_note: Within the merger setting, column 1 of each table (total small-business loans; K6 distress scale) is the headline outcome. The paper's overall preferred specification is the ineligible IBBEA Table 2.

data_access_detail: README: 'The paper relies on confidential data that cannot be disclosed. We provide all relevant codes and mockup datasets (which have the exact same shape as the real datasets, but include only a few rows of made-up data)'. Real sources: NLSY79 with restricted geocodes (BLS agreement), PSID restricted county identifiers, CRA small-business lending (public), NIC/FDIC SOD merger and branch data (public), state macro series (public).
data_files: plus 13 other mock-up .dta files; real-data Stata logs for every table in Log files/
replication_feasible_note: Not from the package (mock-ups). Table 9 could in principle be reconstructed from public CRA, SOD and NIC data by re-implementing Nguyen (2019)'s merger exposure, but that is a substantial independent data build; Table 10 needs restricted PSID geocodes. Author outreach is the realistic route.
priority_note: Eligible merger-exposure design (Tables 9-10, 12 no-controls TWFE columns) but only mock-up data shipped.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text; README title 'Mentally Spent: Credit Conditions and Mental Health' is the working title). Coefficients recorded from the real-data log files. Cohort structure of the merger treatment and whether Treat_Post can switch off need confirmation from the article or authors.
